newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch commercial banks feel scarcity of liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Dutch commercial banks feel scarcity of liquidity.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were under pressure and rose a few basis points on Tuesday, while the market felt it was somewhat short of liquidity due to a scarcity of funds under the current seven-day special advances pact.
"We had needed an allocation of 8.5 billion guilders, while the central bank distributed only 7.5 billion," said one dealer.
Call money was bid at 2.81 percent versus 2.75 percent on Monday and well above the special advances rate of 2.50 percent.
Dealers said commercial banks were eating up some more of their daily credit quota to fill the gap.
The credit quota is set every three months and indicates how much commercial banks can borrow at the secured loans rate, currently 2.00 percent.
"Commercial banks have slid deeper into the red as they have used more of their daily quota today," said one dealer.
Business was "not spectacular" with most trades done at the shorter end in deposits of up to three-months.
The Dutch Finance ministry said this morning it had raised another 1.72 billion guilders through its short-term borrowing programme, Dutch Treasury Certificates.
Dealers said the rates for DTC's was set fairly high at present, as the February contracts were done at 2.98 percent and the March contracts at 3.00 percent.
"This should attract some buyers," said one dealer, adding those rates were expected to come down a little at the start of the new year.
The guilder was steady versus the mark at 112.165 per 100 marks versus 112.16 on Monday.
